HUUM heaters run $773 to $6,278, median $3,203, and the range covers electric units, wood-burning stoves and complete kits — so read what a listing actually includes before comparing two prices.

What is in the range

Thirty-one items. Some are the heater alone, some are packages with stones, a control unit or a flue. That is why a $773 line and a $6,278 line can both be described as a heater. Eight name a 240V supply; the wood-burning stoves need a flue and clearances instead of a circuit.

Sizing and temperature

Ten of the 31 publish a maximum, between 176°F and 230°F. Match output to room volume rather than to the temperature figure: undersized never gets there, oversized cycles hard and wastes power. HUUM's electric units are commonly paired with a separate control unit, which is a second line on the invoice and is easy to miss.

Delivery

A stove is a two-person lift. Free shipping to the lower 48, no minimum, and it stops at the curb — the crate is left at the end of your driveway. Getting it inside is a $600 white-glove upgrade. Getting it inside and assembled is $1,800, which covers everything except electrical work: we recommend you hire a local electrician for that, because the wiring has to meet your local code and pass local inspection. Service fees are non-refundable: if the sauna goes back, the installation does not.
